help.intro: Every German noun belongs to one of three genders — masculine (der), feminine (die) or neuter (das) — and the gender is not about meaning: das Mädchen (the girl) is neuter, der Tisch (the table) is masculine. There is no way round it: you learn every noun together with its article, like a first name and a surname. This quiz is the nominative, the form for the subject of a sentence and after sein: der Mann ist hier, das ist ein Mann. The indefinite article (a/an) is ein for der- and das-words and eine for die-words, and the plural of 'the' is always die, whatever the gender.
help.tips[0].title: der / die / das — and always learn them together
help.tips[0].text: Never memorise 'Tisch = table'. Memorise 'der Tisch'. The app colours nouns by gender (der blue, die red, das green) so the colour sticks with the word.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: the man, the table, the dog
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: the woman, the lamp, the cat
help.tips[0].examples[2].en: the child, the house, the book
help.tips[0].trap: English has no grammatical gender, so nothing in your instinct will tell you a table is 'he'. Only the article you learnt with the word will.
help.tips[0].check.why: It's der Stuhl — masculine. The article is part of the word, so learn them as a pair.
help.tips[0].visual.caption: Three genders and a plural, each with its own article. The colours stay the same everywhere in the course.
help.tips[0].visual.rows[0].label: the
help.tips[1].title: ein for der and das, eine for die
help.tips[1].text: The indefinite article has only two nominative forms: ein (masculine and neuter) and eine (feminine). There is no plural ein — 'apples' is just Äpfel.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: That is a man. That is a house. That is a woman.
help.tips[1].check.why: Lampe is a die-word, and die-words take eine. ein is for der- and das-words.
help.tips[1].visual.caption: ein has no plural: a plural noun simply has no article.
help.tips[1].visual.rows[0].label: the
help.tips[1].visual.rows[1].label: a
help.tips[2].title: No article at all for jobs, nationalities and 'some'
help.tips[2].text: After sein, jobs and nationalities have no article: Ich bin Lehrer. Sie ist Studentin. Er ist Deutscher. Uncountable amounts also take none: Ich esse Brot.
help.tips[2].trap: English says 'I am *a* teacher'. German drops the article — 'Ich bin ein Lehrer' sounds like a line from a film.
help.tips[2].check.why: Jobs after sein take no article in German — just the job: Er ist Arzt.
help.tips[3].title: Endings that give the gender away
help.tips[3].text: die: -e (most), -ung, -heit, -keit, -ion, -schaft. das: -chen, -lein, -ment, -um. der: -er (people and tools), -ling, days, months, seasons. Not perfect, but right far more often than guessing.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: -chen is always das — even for a girl
help.tips[3].check.why: Words ending in -chen are always das — it's die Katze, but das Kätzchen.
help.tips[3].visual.caption: Not a law, but a good bet: the ending often tells you the article.
help.tips[4].title: kein, keine — “not a”, “no”
help.tips[4].text: A noun is negated with kein, never with nicht ein. kein follows the pattern of ein: kein for der and das words (kein Mann, kein Kind), keine for die words and for every plural (keine Frau, keine Kinder).
help.tips[4].examples[0].en: That is not a dog, that is a cat.
help.tips[4].trap: Never nicht ein: “Das ist nicht ein Tisch” is wrong. kein already carries the “not”.
help.tips[4].check.q: Das ist ____ Auto, das ist ein Bus.
help.tips[4].check.why: das Auto takes ein, so its negative is kein.
help.remember[0]: Colour the word in your head: der is blue, die is red, das is green — the whole app uses the same three.
help.remember[1]: Say the article out loud every single time you say a noun. 'Tisch' is not a word; 'der Tisch' is.
help.remember[2]: kein for der/das words, keine for die words and plurals — never nicht ein.
help.context.en: This is my room. The table is brown and the chair is old. The lamp is new. The window is big. And that is a cat – my cat! She's called Mimi.
help.mistakes[0].why: Gender is fixed per noun and has to be learnt with the word.
help.mistakes[1].why: Jobs and nationalities after sein take no article.
help.mistakes[2].why: das-words take ein, exactly like der-words.
help.hook: Every German noun wears a der, die or das — learn the pair together and you'll never have to guess.
